name: promptmaster credit-waste patterns
note: Every pattern is a way a prompt forces a retry, a correction, or a bigger context than the task needs. Retries are the expensive part: each one resends the whole conversation. The audit checks the user's raw prompt against all 35 before anything runs.

families.why: Vagueness makes the model guess. Wrong guesses force retries, and every retry resends the full conversation.

patterns.name: no deliverable named
patterns.signal: The prompt says what topic to work on but not what to produce (a table? a script? a file? a list?).
patterns.fix: Name the artifact: 'one table with columns X, Y, Z', 'a 30-second script', 'a single .md file'.

patterns.name: no audience
patterns.signal: Content is requested with no reader in mind ('write me something for instagram').
patterns.fix: Say who it is for and what they already know: 'a local coffee shop with 8k followers'.

patterns.name: no length or size
patterns.signal: No word count, item count, or duration, so the model picks one and it is wrong.
patterns.fix: Cap it: 'under 400 words', '10 ideas', '3 options max'.

patterns.name: no done-when
patterns.signal: There is no way to tell whether the answer succeeded.
patterns.fix: State the finish line: 'done when I can paste it into the scheduler without edits'.

patterns.name: 'something like' hedging
patterns.signal: 'something like', 'kind of', 'maybe a', 'or whatever' in the ask.
patterns.fix: Commit to one version. You can change it after you see it.

patterns.name: open verdict fishing
patterns.signal: 'thoughts?', 'what do you think?', 'any ideas?' with no decision attached.
patterns.fix: Ask the decision you actually face: 'pick one of these two and say why'.

patterns.name: style matters but no example
patterns.signal: Tone or format matters and no sample is given, guaranteeing a voice miss.
patterns.fix: Paste one short example of the style you want and say 'match this'.

patterns.name: buried constraint
patterns.signal: A hard requirement you already know (budget, tool, deadline) is left out, then revealed after the first wrong answer.
patterns.fix: List every known constraint up front, even the obvious ones.

patterns.name: multiple unrelated asks fused
patterns.signal: Two or three different jobs in one sentence, so each gets a shallow half-answer.
patterns.fix: One prompt per job, or number them and ask for them in order.

patterns.name: 'make it better' with no direction
patterns.signal: Improvement is requested without naming what is wrong.
patterns.fix: Name the failure: 'the hook is weak', 'too formal', 'cut it to half'.

families.why: Saying the same thing twice is pure waste. The second explanation costs tokens and proves the first one leaked.

patterns.name: re-pasting the same context
patterns.signal: The same background paragraph gets pasted into message after message.
patterns.fix: State it once, lock it as a decision, and reference it ('per the locked voice').

patterns.name: restarting instead of continuing
patterns.signal: A fresh chat is opened for a follow-up, so all context must be rebuilt from zero.
patterns.fix: Continue the thread, or carry a 5-line summary + the locked decisions into the new one.

patterns.name: repeating a decision already made
patterns.signal: A preference stated earlier (voice, format, stack) is restated because the model drifted.
patterns.fix: Lock it in decisions.md the first time. Locked decisions are re-applied automatically.

patterns.name: asking the model to recall its own output
patterns.signal: 'like you said before' or 'use the version from earlier' with no quote, forcing a re-derivation.
patterns.fix: Paste the 2 lines you mean. Quoting is cheaper than remembering.

patterns.name: unstated correction loop
patterns.signal: The same class of mistake gets corrected one instance at a time across many messages.
patterns.fix: Correct the rule, not the instance: 'never use em dashes anywhere', then lock it.

families.why: Every pasted token is billed on every following turn. Context you did not need is rent you keep paying.

patterns.name: whole file for a one-function question
patterns.signal: 800 lines pasted when the question is about 20.
patterns.fix: Paste the relevant function plus its callers. Name the file for the rest.

patterns.name: unsummarized transcript dump
patterns.signal: A full meeting transcript or thread pasted raw when only the decisions matter.
patterns.fix: Ask for or write a 10-line summary first, then work from that.

patterns.name: irrelevant attachments
patterns.signal: Docs attached 'just in case' that the task never touches.
patterns.fix: Attach only what the task reads. Mention the rest exists.

patterns.name: screenshot of text
patterns.signal: An error message or config sent as an image, which costs more and reads worse.
patterns.fix: Paste the text itself. Exact characters matter.

patterns.name: paraphrased error message
patterns.signal: 'it says something about a missing module' instead of the actual error.
patterns.fix: Paste the exact error, top line to bottom line.

patterns.name: duplicated instructions
patterns.signal: The same rule appears in the prompt twice in different words, inviting the model to treat them as different rules.
patterns.fix: Say each rule once, in one place.

patterns.name: redundant context
patterns.signal: Background the model already has (from this chat, the repo, or a locked decision) is pasted again anyway.
patterns.fix: Trust what is already in context. Add only what is new.

families.why: When the how is open, the model picks a how. If its pick is wrong you pay for the work twice.

patterns.name: no stack or tool pinned
patterns.signal: A build is requested without naming the language, framework, or tool, so the model chooses and gets corrected.
patterns.fix: Pin it: 'plain HTML + vanilla JS, no frameworks'.

patterns.name: no do-not-touch list
patterns.signal: Nothing marks what must stay unchanged, so working parts get rewritten.
patterns.fix: Say what is frozen: 'do not modify the deploy script or the schema'.

patterns.name: missing environment facts
patterns.signal: OS, versions, or account limits that change the answer are left for the model to assume.
patterns.fix: State them: 'macOS, Node 22, free-tier plan'.

patterns.name: full rewrite when a diff would do
patterns.signal: 'rewrite the whole thing' for a 2-line change, regenerating everything.
patterns.fix: Ask for the edit: 'change only the hook, keep the rest verbatim'.

patterns.name: no output cap on long generation
patterns.signal: An open-ended 'write everything' that produces 3x more than will be read.
patterns.fix: Cap the output and ask for the rest only if needed.

patterns.name: no priority when tradeoffs exist
patterns.signal: Speed, cost, and quality all implied equally, so the model optimizes the wrong one.
patterns.fix: Rank them: 'fast and cheap beats polished here'.

families.why: Messages are the unit of waste. Five turns that could have been one means the context got re-billed five times.

patterns.name: one-question drip
patterns.signal: Related questions asked one message at a time instead of batched.
patterns.fix: Batch them: number 4 questions in one message, get 4 answers in one pass.

patterns.name: permission-seeking turn
patterns.signal: 'can you...?' / 'would it be possible to...?' as its own message before the real ask.
patterns.fix: Just ask the real thing. The capability check is free inside the same message.

patterns.name: resending everything to change one word
patterns.signal: The full prompt is re-pasted with a tiny edit instead of stating the delta.
patterns.fix: Send the delta: 'same as before but the audience is beginners'.

patterns.name: vague rejection
patterns.signal: 'not quite' / 'didn't like it' with no named miss, forcing a blind second attempt.
patterns.fix: Name the miss in one line, and say what to keep.

patterns.name: politeness padding
patterns.signal: Apologies, warm-ups, and sign-offs carrying zero instruction, re-billed every turn after.
patterns.fix: Be direct. Spend the tokens on constraints instead.

families.why: Some turns should never have been prompts at all.

patterns.name: big model for a lookup
patterns.signal: A frontier model asked to spell-check, convert units, or fetch a fact a smaller tool answers.
patterns.fix: Route trivial turns to a small model or a plain tool. Save the big model for judgment.

patterns.name: regenerate instead of edit
patterns.signal: Rerolling the whole answer hoping the one flaw disappears.
patterns.fix: Point at the flaw and ask for a targeted fix of that section only.
